reports.title: Mexico City · six-pair replay and NASA comparison

question: Where does a connected six-pair radar record indicate relative line-of-sight motion?
method: Six descending track 113/frame 079 BETA pairs link seven acquisitions. Native masks, coherence ≥0.30 and accepted fraction ≥0.50 screen samples; delivered ionosphere phase is subtracted. The recorded reference rectangle establishes relative zero. A connected phase network reconstructs acquisition changes and a fitted annual LOS rate. Mixing X05009/X05010 revisions is explicitly enabled for this historical example.
expected: The historical six-pair study reproduced the spatial subsidence pattern in the NASA illustration. It uses the same reference rectangle and a Rainbow scale of −30 to +30 cm/year. Newly generated runs must be checked against the archived numerical evidence; visual agreement alone does not establish geodetic accuracy.
interpret: Start with LOS rate in cm/year. Negative is away from the satellite, positive toward it. A yearly rate is an extrapolated fitted rate over the observed interval, not a full year of observation. Time exploration shows reconstructed acquired epochs. Horizontal and vertical movement are mixed in one LOS measurement.
limits: Reference rectangle: west −99.28, south 19.40, east −99.24, north 19.44. It is retained for reproducibility; coherence cannot establish physical stability. NASA’s reference image is an illustration, not an independent numerical validation grid. BETA calibration and unmodelled atmosphere/unwrapping effects remain.

visual_comparison_note: Compare the broad spatial pattern and the cm/year legends. The app’s rate depends on its reference, screening and phase-network fit. Agreement in appearance does not certify pixel-level velocity accuracy or a vertical-motion estimate.

evidence.label: Qualitative motion-pattern comparison
evidence.description: The fitted relative LOS pattern is consistent with NASA’s illustration over matching dates; no independent displacement grid establishes geodetic accuracy.
evidence.transfer_validation: Not established on an independently held-out event or region.

comparison_review.conclusion: The fitted relative LOS pattern is consistent with NASA’s illustration over matching dates; no independent displacement grid establishes geodetic accuracy.
agrees: Six descending-track 113 pairs connect seven dates over 25 October 2025–17 January 2026, matching the NASA comparison period.
The major relative-motion pattern is visually consistent with the published illustration.
differs: NASA’s article describes monthly rates; the published figure and our opening map use annual rates. Divide cm/year by 12 for cm per mean month; annualization does not extend the 84-day observation record.
Our exact reference rectangle, pair-network fitting, quality masks and processing revisions are documented; NASA’s complete numerical processing/reference solution is not supplied.
unverified: No independent co-registered velocity grid or GNSS measurements: no justified RMSE or speed-accuracy percentage.
The reference is data-suitable, not independently proven stationary; one LOS view cannot separate vertical and horizontal motion.
comparison_review.next_check: Matched independent geodetic observations with compatible LOS projection, dates and a justified reference.
